notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf005:l002: The opening word is unresolved; its initial resembles К rather than Н. The former interpretation as a proper name Nadishin and a claim of geographical origin are not established by the handwriting. Kyrgyz retained provisionally pending a defensible full reading.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf005:l004: The overwritten first word remains provisional. The following words read колдоп жүрчү эле, rather than келген жүргүзүп эле; the object is implicit.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf005:l009: Opening words remain unresolved; neither the proposed Темик nor the interpretation involving laughter is secure. Kyrgyz retained provisionally; the previous fluent English was unsupported.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf005:l017: The opening is provisionally read Урунарга; the internal joins remain indistinct. The former Үрүндө and English reference to an advance were unsupported.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf005:l035: The pale line remains unresolved. Its ending may be өткүр шер rather than отур жер, so the former English about a central land where a sultan sits is not defensible. Kyrgyz retained provisionally; no speculative replacement adopted.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf006:l014: The first word appears to be Коң; the manuscript spelling is uncommon.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf006:l028: The first word reads Казынадай, but its final suffix is visually uncertain.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf005:l001: Completion-first direct transcription and translation from the Sayakbay manuscript image; uncertain readings are explicitly queued for later review.
